newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hails Clinton victory with call for help.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hails Clinton victory with call for help.

text.p: Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui on Wednesday congratulated U.S. president Bill Clinton on his re-election and reminded him that Taipei relies on Washington to keep rival China at bay.
The state Central News Agency said Lee thanked the United States for sending aircraft carriers to the Taiwan strait during communist China's missile tests earlier this year.

Lee made it clear that Taiwan counted on U.S. support in its quest to wriggle free of diplomatic isolation imposed by China, which has regarded the Nationalist-ruled island as a rebel province since a civil war split the two in 1949.
Lee said he hoped Washington could help Taiwan to "take part in international affairs and increase cooperation between the two sides," the message said.
Beijing insists that Taiwan, as a province of China, is not entitled to foreign ties and spurns the 30 states that still recognise Taipei instead of Beijing.
Lee has been at the centre of U.S.-China frictions for more than a year since a private but high-profile visit to his alma mater Cornell University in June 1995 enraged Beijing.

China responded by mounting months of war games that peaked with unarmed missile tests into waters near Taiwan on the eve of the island's March 23 presidential election, a warning to Taiwan not to drop a reunification vow or press for independence.

In a dramatic show of U.S. support for Taiwan, Washington countered China's intimidation by sending two aircraft carriers to nearby waters -- the largest U.S. show of force in the region since the Vietnam War.
